title: Potential ratio bound for Hedge
statement:
Fix $N \ge 1$ experts, a horizon of $T$ rounds, a learning rate $\eta > 0$, and a valid loss sequence $\ell$. Then for every round $t$ with $t < T$, the consecutive potentials satisfy
\[
  \frac{W_{t+1}}{W_t} \;\le\; 1 - \bigl(1 - e^{-\eta}\bigr)\,\widehat{\ell}_t,
\]
where $\widehat{\ell}_t = \sum_{i=1}^{N} p_t(i)\,\ell_t(i)$ is the expected loss of the learner under the Hedge distribution at round $t$.
hypotheses_covered: $\ell$ is a valid loss sequence (all losses in $[0,1]$)
replaced:
For a valid loss sequence and $\eta > 0$, the ratio of consecutive potentials
satisfies
\[
  \frac{W_{t+1}}{W_t} \;\le\; 1 - (1 - e^{-\eta})\,\widehat{\ell}_t,
\]
where $\widehat{\ell}_t = \sum_i p_t(i)\,\ell_t(i)$ is the expected loss at
round $t$.  This is the key potential-ratio lemma of Cesa-Bianchi and Lugosi.
